newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may delay drawing IMF loan to 99-gov source.
newsitem.headline: Russia may delay drawing IMF loan to 99-gov source.

text.p: Russia may delay drawing some of its current $10 billion three-year loan from the International Monetary Fund to 1999 from 1998, a senior government source said on Tuesday.

The source said Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin had agreed the delay with the finance ministry because of possible funding problems in 1999, but the cabinet would take a final decision on Thursday.

The proposed delay in drawing the IMF Extended Fund Facility would involve Russia receiving $2.0 billion in 1998 and $1.0 billion in 1999, instead of the currently planned $2.6 billion in 1998 and $400 million in 1999, the source said.
But Russia would borrow $1.1 billion from the World Bank in 1998, he said.

Russia is still negotiating with the World Bank about a loan to help restructure the coal industry, he said, but it hoped to receive $200 million from this loan this year and $300 million in 1998. He did not make it clear whether this was part of the planned $1.1 billion borrowing from the bank.

The IMF is currently disbursing the Extended Fund Facility on a quarterly basis after quarterly reviews of the Russian economy. The IMF board is due to meet on September 3 to discuss disbursing the latest tranche, after an IMF mission this month came away with largely positive conclusions.
